body:
[aida:product] #2033 FINDING: the reviewer's remedy cannot be built. Five fixtures, five negatives, and the fifth explains WHY rather than just failing.

RAN THE FIFTH AS RULED. It is the one that settles it, because it fails in the opposite direction from the first four and the mechanism is now visible.

    FIXTURE                          list       show      ratio   verdict
    3 objects, 1.2 MB, MUTATED       139 ms     250 ms    1.79    passes — no signal
    500 objects, 176 KB, fixed        90 ms      96 ms    1.07    baseline
    500 objects, 176 KB, MUTATED      91 ms     153 ms    1.68    passes — no signal
    500 objects, 9.96 MB, FIXED     1.089 s    1.075 s    0.99    FAILS ON CORRECT CODE
    (that last fixture takes 346 s — 5.8 minutes — to run)

THE FIFTH IS THE ANSWER. Look at `list` in that row: 1.089 s. THE CACHE-BACKED BASELINE IS AS SLOW AS THE COMMAND UNDER TEST. `show` is actually marginally FASTER — ratio 0.99.

So the dimensions that make a full store load expensive make the CACHED path expensive too. The ratio cannot separate them because both surfaces pay the same dominant cost, and the absolute 1000 ms ceiling then fires on CORRECT code — the test fails the fix it was written to protect.

THE SHAPE IS UNWORKABLE ON EVERY AXIS SIMULTANEOUSLY:
  small fixture   no signal            1.68x–1.79x, under any bound worth setting
  large fixture   no discrimination    ratio 0.99, and the ceiling false-fails correct code
  large fixture   not CI-viable        346 s to run, against a ~9–10 min total CI cycle

There is no middle setting that escapes all three, because the two failure modes move in opposite directions as the fixture grows.

I AM NOT PUSHING ANYTHING TO #2033. Per your ruling I am not substituting a different design quietly, and per TASK-1418 I am not shipping a guard that has never been demonstrated to fire. Four green fixtures are four instruments that were never live, not four pieces of evidence the code is fine. The branch is rebased in a worktree and unpushed; the PR is exactly as codex left it.

WHAT I PROPOSE, and it needs no new tooling: the acceptance criteria ALREADY NAME THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT.

    aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events

That measures the real store under real use, which is the only place the dominant term has been shown to exist. It is criterion 5 of BUG-1480, written before any of this. The answer to the reviewer is not a better fixture — it is that the criterion already specifies the correct instrument and CI is the wrong place to run it.

I CAN OFFER ONE THING THE SOURCE CHECK DID NOT: the existing guard greps this crate's own source for the absence of a substring. If a structural guard is wanted, a materially better one is available — assert that the show path does not call `load()` by a means the compiler enforces rather than by substring. But that is a design proposal, not a rework, and it is yours and the reviewer's to accept or reject.

ONE THING I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. `list` being slow on the fifth fixture is itself interesting and I have a hypothesis about it. I am not chasing it: you ruled run-the-fifth-then-stop, it is BUG-1480's diagnostic work rather than #2033's review, and I have already handed you one derived-not-measured number tonight. If you want it measured, say so and I will do it as its own task.

STOPPING AND REPORTING AS RULED. Two of three assigned merged — #2026 at 62a1396adf, #2027 at 8bc2512480. #2033 ends in a measured argument rather than a merged test, which I believe is the correct outcome when the requested remedy cannot be built.
subject: #2033 FINDING: five fixtures, five negatives — the large fixture makes the CACHED baseline equally slow (ratio 0.99) and false-fails correct code; remedy as specified cannot be built
